content.text:
Quoted Content-Type parameter values now parse per RFC 9110, and all 118 tests in the content-type, content-parser, custom-parser and content-length files pass, along with lint.

The fix is in `lib/content-type.js`:

- **Quoted values:** the parameter regex now accepts a quoted-string (with backslash escapes) as a whole. `boundary="part;one"` gives `part;one`, and `charset=utf-8` after it is still parsed.
- **Nested text:** `title="lang=en; charset=latin1"` yields only `title`, with no `charset` or `lang` parameter.
- **Junk after a closing quote:** it is skipped up to the next `;`, and quoted strings inside that junk are skipped too.
- **Escapes:** `\"` and `\\` are unescaped when parsing and re-escaped in `toString()`. Before, `toString()` didn't escape them, so a value containing `"` would not have round-tripped.

I added tests to `test/content-type.test.js` covering the two cases from the report, escaped quotes, junk after a quoted value, and the `toString()` round-trip.

- **Junk after a closing quote:** it is skipped up to the next `;`, and quoted strings inside that junk are skipped too.
- **Escapes:** `\"` and `\\` are unescaped when parsing and re-escaped in `toString()`. Before, `toString()` didn't escape them, so a value containing `"` would not have round-tripped.
